note.p: The core element in this group of names - including both Crump and Crumpe and Miss and Mrs Crumpe is Miss Crumpe, the author of Geraldine of Desmond, published in three volumes in 1829, and much noticed in the Morning Post, and advertised in 1831 (suggesting her presence in London). She was the daughter of Samuel Crumpe (1776-96 - who married Susan Ingram in 1792)) a doctor who died of cholera responding to the illness of a women he saw in the street. He was also an expert in the uses of opium, publishing on the subject. The family were based in Ireland but appear to have visited London for a period (some 30+ years after Samuel's death). The challenge is identifying a male member of the family, since Samuel Crumpe's only son died in childhood. However, he came from a family of six, and it is possible a brother in law or cousin was in attendance.
It is possible there is no male. Miss Crump is the first of the entries, and he may then abbreviate; but there is no clear pattern.

There is a suggesive but probably unconnected report in 18 July 1833 in the Morning Post about several members of a Crumpe family drowning following the capsizing of their boat off the Isla of Man. And an entry on Fashionable departures for July 8 1833 of Miss Crumpe to Liverpool.
